title: Ancient Greece and democracy
examples: How did the people in Athens make decisions together?
What were the main differences between Athens and Sparta?
Why was voting only for certain people in ancient Greece?

explain.say: Today we learn about ancient Greece and its two famous city-states.
Athens was known for its culture and its system of democracy.
Sparta, by contrast, was famous for its strong military training and discipline.
In Athenian democracy, male citizens could vote on laws and decisions.

items: They voted on laws in the assembly.

explain.say: The ancient Olympic Games were held to celebrate athletic skill and honor the gods.
In our modern life, we see democracy when we vote for local council representatives.

faq.q: Was Athenian democracy exactly like democracy today?
faq.a: No, Athenian democracy was much more limited than ours. Only free-born male citizens could participate in voting and government.
asks: Were all people allowed to vote in Athens?
What were the rules for voting in ancient Athens?

faq.q: What was the main difference between Athens and Sparta?
faq.a: Athens focused on arts, philosophy, and democracy, while Sparta focused entirely on creating strong soldiers.
asks: Which city was more focused on fighting?
What did the people of Sparta value most?

faq.q: Who could participate in the ancient Olympic Games?
faq.a: The games were primarily for male athletes from different Greek city-states. They celebrated physical excellence.
asks: Were women allowed to compete in the Olympics?
What was the purpose of the ancient Olympics?

faq.q: Did all people in ancient Greece have the right to vote?
faq.a: No, women, slaves, and foreigners were generally excluded from the voting process in Athenian democracy.
asks: Were there restrictions on citizenship rights?
Who did not count as a citizen in Athens?

faq.q: Why was Sparta so focused on the military?
faq.a: Sparta's entire way of life was structured around producing loyal and highly skilled soldiers for their state.
asks: What was the purpose of the Spartan education system?
Why did Sparta train its men so rigorously?

facts: Athens was famous for its advancements in philosophy and art.
Sparta was renowned throughout Greece for its disciplined army.
In Athenian democracy, citizens gathered in the assembly to vote.
The ancient Olympic Games honored athletic prowess and the gods.

quiz.say: Which city-state was known for its strong military focus?
quiz.why: Sparta's entire culture revolved around military training and discipline.

wrong.0: The Olympics were an event, not a city-state.
wrong.1: Citizens were the people who participated, not the place itself.
wrong.3: Athens was more famous for its culture and democracy.

quiz.say: What was a key requirement for voting in Athenian democracy?
quiz.why: Only free-born male citizens had the right to vote in the Athenian assembly.

wrong.0: The system was very exclusive regarding who counted as a citizen.
wrong.2: The system excluded women and foreigners from voting.
wrong.3: Voting rights were based on citizenship, not just money.

quiz.say: The ancient Olympics were held mainly to celebrate:
quiz.why: The games were an ancient festival honoring physical ability and the gods.

wrong.0: Art was important, but the games were specifically about sports.
wrong.2: The focus was on physical contests, not political debate.
wrong.3: While Sparta was strong, the games celebrated individual athletic feats.
